name: Tlazoyaltepec Mixtec
confidence_why: No description of Tlazoyaltepec Mixtec stress exists; the only statement that covers the variety is Josserand's 1983 family-wide claim that the Mixtec couplet is stressed on its first syllable, known only through Carroll 2015 and Penner 2019, so any placement here is inferred from relatives such as neighbouring Peñoles (penultimate stress, Daly & Daly 1977) rather than observed.

catalog_quote: The couplet is “the nucleus of the phonological word and usually the stem of the grammatical word” (E. V. Pike & Cowan 1967:1). The couplet’s morphological basis is the minimal word and canonical root, both of which are bimoraic across Mixtec varieties. However, the couplet is not necessarily equivalent to either the word or the root. ... Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. Besides the data from Santo Domingo Nuxaa shown in (4.2), several other descriptions support the characterization of stress in Mixtec as falling on the first vowel of the couplet. ... In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. ... Furthermore, one Mixtec variety, that of Yoloxochitl (Yol) has been described to have final stress, partially on the basis of these same distributional properties (DiCanio p.c., DiCanio et al. submitted).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened the full thesis (362 pp.) with extracted text; printed p. 86 = p. 108 reads verbatim: 'Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.' The saved excerpt matches it. The rest of the section (Carroll sec. 4.2.1, pp. 85-86) is a survey of first-syllable-of-couplet stress in Ayutla, Jicaltepec/Pinotepa, Acatlan, Diuxi, Mixtepec, Atatlahuca, Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala and Nuxaa; sec. 4.2.2 (p. 87) notes Yoloxochitl as the one variety described with final stress. None of these is Tlazoyaltepec. Identity…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable of the bimoraic root 'couplet' (the disyllabic stem that is the nucleus of the Mixtec word), i.e. on the penult of a bare disyllabic root; clitics and affixes outside the couplet are unstressed. This is Josserand's generalization over her whole dialect survey (which includes Santiago Tlazoyaltepec as town 'Tlaz'), not a statement made for Tlazoyaltepec specifically.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the quoted generalization asserts uniform behaviour across Mixtec varieties.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the couplet (root/stem), which is normally the whole phonological word minus clitics. The nearest described sister variety, Santa María Peñoles (Daly & Daly 1977 ALIM 3, p. 19, page scan held by the project at, states the same rule in morpheme terms: 'El acento se localiza en la penúltima sílaba de los morfemas de dos o más sílabas' (stress on the penultimate syllable of morphemes of two or more syllables), with monosyllabic clitics attached by hyphen; but that is peno1244, not tlaz1235.
new_statements.identity_note: Santiago Tlazoyaltepec, distrito Etla, Oaxaca (ISO mqh). Glottolog 5.3 lists 0 descriptive works; INALI files the municipality under the variant tu'un dau <mixteco bajo de Valles>; Ethnologue/Wikipedia (after Egland & Bartholomew 1983) treat it as a dialect of 'Estetla Mixtec' together with Santa María Peñoles (mil, peno1244), San Antonio Huitepec (mxs, huit1252) and San Juan Tamazola (vmx, tama1339) at c. 75% mutual intelligibility. The only first-hand stress statement in the group is for Peñoles (Daly & Daly 1977:19, penultimate syllable of morphemes of 2+ syllables), which is peno1244, not tlaz1235. The quoted statement is Josserand's pan-Mixtec couplet generalization (survey includes Tlazoyaltepec as town 'Tlaz'), reported second-hand in Carroll 2015:86.
